learning: If max_error stays near 0.063 m at base_speed 1.0, speed is not the limit and the next lever is wheel_track. If line_loss returns to 0 on oval and slalom, the iteration-2 controller was the cause of the line loss, and the sensor y and inertia change can stay.
notes: Geometry held at the iteration-2 values as the Builder requested. Controller softened to kp 3.5 and base_speed 1.0 to cut the line-loss and oscillation seen in iteration 2, while kd stays at 0.6 for damping.
rationale: Race evidence from iteration 2 (entityR2A geometry with kp 4.0 and kd 0.6, score 114.36 vs 111.80) is mixed. Line loss rose on oval (0.25 per run) and slalom (0.30), up from 0 and 0.1 in iteration 1. Max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.064 m on every track, so the gain increase did not reduce the limiting error. Steering oscillation rose on the s-bend (0.28 from 0.13), which means kp 4 with kd 0.6 is pushing the loop toward overshoot. Progress fell on oval (0.55 to 0.32) and slalom (0.10 to 0.09). The Builder asked me to hold geometry, so the geometry is the iteration-2 values unchanged. The controller must now do the work. I am lowering kp from 4.0 to 3.5 to cut overshoot and the line-loss excursions it causes. I am keeping kd at 0.6 for damping. The constant max_error near 0.063 m across all three tracks, and the steady 0.02 to 0.03 m rms_error, suggest the robot is entering bends too fast for its correction, so I am lowering base_speed from 1.2 to 1.0 to give the loop more time to respond. ki stays at 0.05 because there is no sign of a steady offset, and the sensor weights stay at -2 to +2 for the 0.03 m spacing. line_loss stays last_direction, which has held up in every race. Expected result, not yet measured: fewer line-loss events on oval and slalom, and max_error pulled below 0.06 m on more trials. If line loss stays at 0.2 or higher on oval or slalom, the cause is the reduced inertia or the closer sensors, which is the Builder's next revert candidate.
